New in this edition · applied Administrative Officer scenarios. Q1151–1300 add 150 applied scenarios organised as 15 linked cases of ten decisions each (Cases 61–75), written for the working desk of an Administrative Officer rather than for recall alone. Every scenario sits inside the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965. Sections 27–30 run from competence and the charge-sheet, through the conduct of the inquiry and minor-penalty files, to final orders, appeals, revision and review, and then to what follows after the order: a set-aside, the disciplinary record, pay and duty status, and pension. Linked rules appear only where they operate on a CCS (CCA) order. Every scenario keeps the original format: four options, one best answer, a cited basis, reasoning, and the specific trap that separates a defensible order from a quashed one. The underlying bank (Q1–1150) is unchanged, so earlier progress and answer positions remain valid.
Scope of the applied set (revised 7 November 2026). All 150 applied scenarios in Q1151–1300 sit inside the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965. Other instruments appear only where they operate directly on a CCS (CCA) order: FR 54 and FR 54-B for the pay and duty treatment of a suspension period, FR 53 for subsistence, the pension rules for the effect of a Rule 11 penalty or a continuing proceeding at retirement, the Conduct Rules for the Rule 14(2) complaints-committee proviso, and the access rules for a request for the inquiry record. Forty earlier items, in four cases, turned on the RTI Act, leave and LTC as free-standing subjects. They were withdrawn and replaced by the cases on a set-aside, the disciplinary record, pay and pension; Q1251–1260 also became the revision-and-review case, because the older block began there. Those fifty numbers therefore carry different questions, and any answers recorded against Q1251–1300 before the revision no longer correspond. Clear them once: open Reattempt this batch on batch 26. Q1151–1250 and the whole audited bank (Q1–1150) are unaffected.

Parts & Schedule — one-line revision map

9 Parts in the Rules; 1 attached Schedule with 5 Parts. The official divisions are called Parts, rather than chapters. Practice Q1101–1150 through the collection selector.

Rules Part and official titleRule coverageOne-line meaning
Part I — GeneralRules 1–3Short title, commencement, interpretation and application.
Part II — ClassificationRules 4–7, including 6-AClassification and constitution of services/posts, class-to-group references and General Central Service.
Part III — Appointing AuthorityRules 8–9Appointment powers for Group A and other services/posts.

The Schedule: five internal Parts

Schedule Part and headingOne-line meaning
Part I — Central Civil Services, Group ALists Central Civil Services, Group A.
Part II — Central Civil Services, Group B (except civilians in Defence Services)Identifies the covered Group B services and applicable authority/penalty entries, excluding defence civilians.
Part III — Central Civil Services, Group C (except civilians in Defence Services)Identifies the covered Group C services and applicable authority/penalty entries, excluding defence civilians.
Part IV — Central Civil Services, Group D (except civilians in Defence Services)Preserves the legacy Group D Schedule heading and entries; not a claim of universal present-day Group D recruitment.
Part V — Civil Posts in Defence ServicesContains the applicable defence-civilian post and authority/penalty entries; not the armed-forces disciplinary codes.

Part IV of the Schedule retains the legacy Group D heading in the source: it is not a statement that all present-day posts are recruited/classified as Group D. Defence-civilian exclusions and current applicable authority amendments must be checked. Department-specific orders may have their own Schedules; do not add their internal divisions to this count. Rule 32 is omitted; lettered rules 6-A and 29-A do not create extra Parts. Source: [S1], arrangement and Schedule, read with applicable overlays.

Applied AO scenarios — how to use Q1151–1300

What the set is. Fifteen linked cases of ten decisions each. Each case gives the shared facts, then ten independent decisions that move through one file the way a real desk does: who may act, what the paper must show, which clock applies, and what the order must say. The correct option is always the one that is lawful on the stated facts alone; the distractors are the shortcuts that actually get orders quashed.

1 · Competence
Who holds the power? Check the Group, the appointing authority, Rule 12(4), the Schedule or delegation, and whether the signatory actually holds statutory power.
2 · Procedure
Which route applies — Rule 14, Rule 16, Rule 19, Rule 20/21, Rule 27 or Rule 29 — and which safeguard (documents, advice, representation) is triggered at this stage?
3 · Reasons
What must appear on the face of the order: findings on each article, disagreement reasons, non-acceptance of advice, the extent and duration of a withholding, and the mode of service?
Three-pass drill. Pass 1 — exam conditions: one case (10 decisions) in eight minutes, no scrolling back. Pass 2 — read every explanation and write down only the trap. Pass 3 — return after a week and answer with the rule citation covered. For a full mock, select “Mixed set 24–26”, or use “Applied AO desk · Q1151–1300” in exam mode: 50 decisions in 40 minutes is a realistic pace. Use “Export a case as a finished file” when you have closed a case: it writes out the ten decisions, your answers, the key and the score.

Ten errors that cost orders

  1. An order signed by someone who does not hold the statutory power, including officers on current duty charge.
  2. Treating a Review Committee recommendation as the order extending suspension under Rule 10(6).
  3. Forgetting that the 270-day and two-year no-charge-sheet ceilings under Rule 10(7) run independently of timely reviews.
  4. A charge memo that states conclusions instead of definite articles, facts, documents and witnesses under Rule 14(3).
  5. Refusing a requisitioned document without a written reason, or compelling production after a public-interest certificate.
  6. Disagreeing with an exoneration in the final order without first disclosing the tentative reasons under Rule 15(2).
  7. Enclosing Commission advice with the penalty order instead of the pre-decision fifteen-day response under Rule 15(3)(b).
  8. Using the Group A/B Presidential forum for Group C/D staff, or appealing an order made by the President.
  9. Commencing revision while the appeal limitation is still running, contrary to Rule 29(2).
  10. Withholding gratuity on “contemplation” of proceedings rather than on proceedings actually instituted.
  11. Serving a penalty order without recording the date of delivery, so the Rule 25 clock cannot be proved.

Every scenario states its assumptions inside the case context. If a live file differs on any stated assumption — the Group, the appointing authority, the stage, or whether an inquiry was held — re-run the three-step audit rather than lifting the answer.

    DoPT-issued compilation obtained as a reproduced PDF, not downloaded from an official host. Checked alongside suspension material in the 26 March 2024 consolidation [S4].     Open reference copy: Rule 10 · Rule 11 · Rule 12 · Rule 14 · Rule 15 · Rule 16 · Rule 24 · Rule 29 / 29-A. These are third-party reproductions: check the Gazette copy before relying on a figure in a live file.

  10. [S10] Linked instruments used only where a CCS (CCA) order touches them: CCS (Pension) Rules 2021; FR 53; FR 54-B

    Used only where a linked rule operates directly on a CCS (CCA) order, chiefly in Case 72–75: how a pension record follows a set-aside penalty, a penalty in force at retirement, a proceeding continuing after retirement, and the treatment of a suspension period. FR 53 and FR 54-B remain the source for subsistence and regularisation. The RTI Act, leave and LTC are deliberately outside this set: they are not CCS (CCA) subjects, and the audited bank already covers the suspension-compendium material on them.

    Not a substitute for the departmental rule book: pension figures can be altered by later instructions, and the NPS/UPS position of a given post must be verified separately.

Full-compendium scope and currency

The added collection deliberately extends beyond CCS (CCA): FR 53 governs subsistence, FR 54-B regularisation and death, FR 55 leave, and the cited Pension Rules govern specified retirement questions. The 2022 information document is a consolidation of sources, not a standalone amendment. Its older authority wording must be read with the verified January 2026 amendment. Historical one-year guidance cannot override an applicable later statutory no-charge-sheet ceiling. Pension questions assume CCS (Pension) Rules 2021 applicability; they do not settle NPS/UPS contribution issues. Old criminal-code citations are tested only as historical wording in the document. The addition covers A–Z subject headings, not every possible subcase or all later judicial developments.

How to read the labels

Statutory rule identifies a rule-based proposition. Government instruction identifies a cited executive instruction, sometimes reproducing a judicial principle; it is not presented as additional statutory wording. Department-specific order / Schedule should not be applied to a different employer or cadre without the governing authority instrument.

Checklist framing note

The submitted question was adapted at Q407, with related cases throughout Q360–433. Suspension validity, misconduct gravity and punishment quantum are not a universal Rule 29/29-A checklist. Rule 27(2) expressly addresses procedure, evidence and penalty in a penalty appeal. Rule 29 adds revisional competence, timing and safeguards; Rule 29-A is Presidential and requires qualifying new material. Workflow questions do not invent a rigid statutory sequence where none is prescribed.

High-value currency checks

  • Rule 14(4)(b): initial 15-day defence period; reasoned extensions up to 15 days at a time; overall 45 days from receipt.
  • Rule 14(13): produce requisitioned records or issue a non-availability certificate within one month; separate public-interest/security withholding proviso.
  • Rule 14(24): six-month inquiry/report period from receipt of appointment order; reasoned extensions not exceeding six months at a time.
  • Current Rule 15: report response in (2); necessary advice procedure in (3); final findings in (4); minor/major disposal in (5)/(6).
  • Rule 16: advice response in (1)(d), findings in (1)(e); inquiry incorporation extends through Rule 14(24).
  • Rule 32: omitted. Do not use an older operative Rule 32 citation in place of the surviving safeguards.
  • Rule 10(7): separate 90-day review, up-to-180-day extension and conditional no-departmental-charge-sheet total-ceiling checks.

Scope limitation: The Schedule treatment is selective and exam-focused, not an exhaustive replacement Schedule. Classification references reproduce statutory wording where relevant; historical Group D references do not assert a present recruitment classification for every post. Case assumptions govern the MCQ; actual orders require the applicable institutional rules, delegations and up-to-date legal advice.
